title: Multinomial logistic regression for an unordered categorical outcome
summary: One log relative-risk ratio per non-reference category of a nominal outcome, with an explicitly chosen reference category.
_learn_page_pending: No Learn page on askmallard.com covers multinomial regression yet. `learn` names the page that is planned for it.

sizing._why: No multinomial form is in the catalog; sizing needs the anticipated distribution across all categories in each group and is a simulation.

pinned_defaults: R: the reference level written out (home). factor() on text puts it first only if it sorts first alphabetically.
R: multinom(maxit = 1000, reltol = 1e-14). At the defaults (100 iterations, loose tolerance) the coefficients stopped 2.45e-4 short of the maximum on this fixture.
Python: MNLogit takes the LOWEST code as the reference, so the codes are assigned explicitly (home = 0). Newton at tol 1e-12, convergence asserted.
_nominal_not_ordinal: Use this model when the categories have no order. When they do (none, mild, moderate, severe), a proportional-odds model uses that order and is more efficient (ordinal-proportional-odds).
